expectations.text: The endpoint is created with MapPost and accepts IFormFile (or a streamed body) with antiforgery handled explicitly
expectations.evidence: Uses app.MapPost("/api/contracts", async (IFormFile file) => ...) and explicitly calls .DisableAntiforgery() with a comment explaining why (cookie-less, unauthenticated API) and what to do if cookie auth is added.

expectations.text: Size is limited to 5 MB and content is verified as PDF by its signature, not only by extension or Content-Type
expectations.evidence: MaxFileBytes = 5*1024*1024 is enforced in the handler (413), and Kestrel and FormOptions limits are set. The handler reads the first 5 bytes and compares them to "%PDF-". Curl showed a .pdf file containing 'hello' returned 400.

expectations.text: Files are saved under ./uploads with a server-generated name
expectations.evidence: The handler writes to Path.Combine("uploads", $"{Guid.NewGuid()}.pdf") after Directory.CreateDirectory("uploads"). The client file name is never used. The curl test listed a GUID-named file in uploads.

expectations.text: Failures return problem-details responses with correct status codes (400, 413 or 415)
expectations.evidence: The handler uses Results.Problem with 400, 413 and 415. AddProblemDetails and UseStatusCodePages are configured. Curl returned problem JSON with 400 and 415. The Kestrel 413 was also problem-details JSON ({"title":"Payload Too Large","status":413}), though it had no detail field.
